Shri Rajendra Singh Yadav - Advocate for the applicant
 Shri K S Tomar- Public Prosecutor for respondent/State
 Shri Girraj Soni - Advocate for complainant.

Order 
This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of B.N.S.S/S.439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail.

He has been arrested on 08.09.2024 in connection with Crime No.319 of 2024 registered at Police Station Dehat, District Bhind for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

As per prosecution story, an agreement to sale of agricultural land was executed by applicant and Ajan Singh showing themselves as owners of the said land for a consideration of Rs.45,00,000/-
with complainant.

As per the agreement, the sale deed was to be registered within eleven months,
but prior to that the complainant came to know that the accused were not the actual owners of the said land and they had cheated him by showing forged and fabricated documents and taken Rs.20,00,000/- in advance from him.
On the basis of such allegation, the present F.I.R. has been registered against applicant and co-accused.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is aged around NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:2681 2 MCRC-928-2025 55 years.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that there is no part of the applicant in the commission of alleged offence as admittedly, out of an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- allegedly given to the applicant,

1 Rs.10,00,000/- had been deposited in the amount of co-accused and no cash had been recovered from him.
It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of District Bhind and there is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Confinement may bring his social disrepute and personal inconvenience.
It is further submitted that there is no criminal history against applicant.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in the investigation/trial and would not be a source of embarrassment and harassment in any manner to the complainant party side.
The applicant is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by this Court in case of grant of bail.
On the basis of the above submissions, the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the complainant had vehemently opposed the present bail application and had prayed for its rejection.

After considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as contentions of the parties and the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pretrial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant on stringent condition of depositing a part of the embezzled amount.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:2681 3 MCRC-928-2025 with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for her appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant :-
1.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
